flags.summary: A setter confirmed on a recorded team call that he sends prospects voice messages in the persona of Trevor, the coach they are being sold; a closer and the sales manager both treated this as routine.
evidence: And you're Trevor, right? Like, you're Trevor. Just to check.
I'm Trevor? What do you mean?
Yeah. As in, like, you talk as Trevor in the VMs.
Oh, yeah. I talk as Trevor.
Okay. It's good to know. Perfect.
Sweet. Awesome. Good stuff.

flags.summary: Deposits and six-instalment payment plans are referenced internally as normal deal mechanics, two days after the same closer told a prospect on a live call that nothing about instalments is set in stone.
evidence: I thought I was going to lose a deposit, there's a big chance I can still get him in on Friday, because he cannot pay [in] six times
Well, I've got the deposit that's like 99% coming in. I'm definitely going to still get them in.
Otherwise, I'm gonna make a plan with him that he starts next month or something, but he is still going to join someday.

We don't have anything, like, set in stone. It's like, this is exactly what we can also do. If we do have to go off of doing it in just some one go, we would just have a conversation about it and see what would work.

flags.summary: Recreational stimulant use as a closing aid was raised on a team call and the sales manager's stated position was that reps may do what they feel is necessary provided KPIs are met.
evidence: Only cocaine. What? Yeah, only cocaine. If you guys are going to use drugs, you might as well go for the non- ones. Just kidding.

I had a friend that he told me that when he was closing, the best performance he had on a little line of cocaine and a beer. He was closing like crazy. I don't know. I haven't tried that, but everything is possible.

You guys are all 100% in control of your own decisions, of how you go about things. I am not an advocate for anything that would put anybody in actual harm, but as long as you abide by the KPI, you abide by the standards of the team, you are free to do what you feel is necessary.
Nothing. Nothing, dude. Nothing. I do have mushrooms. I haven't taken them yet, though.

flags.summary: A closer characterised a prospect's disclosed risk of harming himself and others at work as what made him easy to close, with no reference to the clinical or safety substance of the disclosure.
evidence: I had this call yesterday with a firefighter. Like, he was like, yeah, I'm just, I'm really not showing up well. I'm not helping the people. Like, I'm putting other people at risk. It's so easy to then close them.
As in, like, he isn't fit. So he is putting other people's lives in danger.
And then it's like, then it's an easy close, like you still have to do everything, but someone like that is like in

flags.summary: Prospect phone numbers captured at booking are not reaching the closers' system, so DM-set calls cannot be pre-confirmed and no-shows are being generated by a data-plumbing fault.
evidence: How do we do it with me now connecting with a lead if Adam books him in? Because I don't get a phone number.
literally on the thing where I have to set, it asks me to put a phone number
It does say the attendee, but it doesn't say their phone number, not in Close. If I click on their name, that's when you can see someone's phone number, but I also don't see any phone number here.
Yeah, we probably want to start getting a phone number down when you're booking it in.
